title: Day 18 Making a Three.js Game with No Game Dev Experience
author: TimeForsaken5275
selftext:
Full Budget: $200. I vibecode this javascript game 80 hrs per week. Context: I'm an unemployed almost in poverty college student, I'm praying hopefully this is a good 3rd project on my resume so I can get my first tech internship soon, im a junior in USA. 

It feels like the Great Depression to get a white collar job here in the USA as a Gen Z Male with absolutely no wealthy connections, but I'm trying my best everyday

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body:
Free advice: Games won't get you a tech internship unless they're really, really interesting or have crazy virality. It's debatable whether they'd even get you an internship at a games company these days. 

Try to build a product instead. Identify a problem in business, solve that problem, *market* the problem. It can be any problem. Find people with problems, solve those problems. Hard problems.

comments.author: kallekul
comments.body:
Cool! So, you've let AI build a game that's entirely based on an existing, well-defined game. Some questions, because you need to understand what it takes to get a job in game dev/tech (if that's what you're trying to do), and be honest about whether you're getting closer to becoming attractive on the job market:  
  
First of all, why are you not mentioning that this is a CS clone/rip-off?  
Why would someone hire you based on this project, do you think?  
What skills are you showcasing with this project, do you think?  
What are you studying at college?

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body: These are all very good questions, OP. Don't get eager to throw punches. Actually sit down with a piece of paper and think through kallekul's questions as if they were being asked to you in an interview, they are *excellent*.

replies.author: kallekul
replies.body:
Eh, I disagree. It's obviously not the most useless thing he could do, but not the most useful. Of course, it's good to start anywhere as long as you get started. But these kind of project are kind of lacking in substance if you don't know what you're doing or what your goal is.  
And yes, he didn't specify he was trying to get into game dev, which is why I said "if that's what you're trying to do".

comments.author: CaptainCactus124
comments.body:
Hey i work as a manager in game codev space, working on backends for AAA games.

While this is cool, and demonstrates passion and drive, its not going to really get my intention alone.

If you cannot code, you dont get hired at my place. If you cannot explain the systems and code from a technical standpoint of this project, you won't get hired. Why? Because ai gets you 80 percent of the way there in 30x less time but that last 20 percent separates the people who can code and know what they are looking at from people who cant.

You didnt mention anything about your actual technical skills so just dismiss me if you got this covered

comments.author: Maleficent_Public621
comments.body:
Out of curiosity, is this game 100% built in javascript? Did you legitimately port the game to the browser? 

Did you give it the source code for the game as context? How did you recreate the game mode 1:1?

I don't think this will land you a job out the gate, but it's kind of interesting that you basically ported CS2 to the browser lol. I interview people pretty often (I do mostly full stack web app/ios app development) and I'd be impressed if you could tell me how the system itself was designed, and how you prompted to get an output like this.

comments.author: Alone-Leg-1281
comments.body:
Those assets look a exactly like cs2 assets you might get a cease and desist from Valve when you try and publish this. Valve has done this in the past there is precedence for this you just need to google. 

A browser version of a popular game is prooobably not as good as a native binary + infra that valve has built to support cs-go. webgpu and webgl are impressive pieces of tech and they can do a lot but at the end of the day javascript is still an interpreted runtime. websockets are not as good as tcp/udp for this type of network traffic. people care a lot about latency with competitive shooters. I guess it can be a good resuma piece if you can spin it in the right way.
